title: Propagation Genealogy, Lot Traceability & Breach Reconstruction

content.overview: Specialist instruction for propagation genealogy, lot traceability & breach reconstruction in propagation and clean-stock operations.

sections.title: Traceability connects source to downstream exposure
sections.body: Donor/accession ID, cutting batch, tray/cell identity, operator, date and handoff destination create the chain needed to find potentially related material when a biosecurity concern appears.

sections.title: A traceability break is itself a controlled deviation
sections.body: Unlabeled or conflicting material should not be repaired by guesswork. The record should preserve the discrepancy, containment step and evidence used to resolve or disposition the affected material.

sections.title: Reconstruction narrows containment
sections.body: Good genealogy can identify which lots, trays, tools, work periods or destinations share a plausible connection, allowing investigation to be targeted while preserving uncertainty about actual transmission.

commonMistakes: Using cultivar name as the only identity field.
Guessing the identity of a tray after a label break.
Discarding movement history once a batch is handed off.
content.practicalApplication: Given a donor-to-handoff genealogy with one missing label and one later concern, reconstruct the affected chain, identify material that should be held pending review and state what cannot be concluded.
content.summary: Traceability makes containment and investigation reconstructable without turning association into proof of transmission.
